title: Why Your Student Loan Balance Keeps Growing
hook_text: WHY YOUR LOAN BALANCE IS GROWING

beats.say: You've been making your student loan payments for 5 years, so why is your total balance higher than the day you graduated?
beats.visual: A close-up of a person's hands holding a heavy wooden graduation diploma frame in a dimly lit room with side light.

beats.say: You chose an income-driven repayment plan to keep your monthly bills affordable on an entry-level salary.
beats.visual: A dark wooden desk with a vintage metal pen resting beside a blank white paper pad under warm desk lamp light.

beats.say: How does a monthly payment leave your principal higher year after year?
beats.visual: A macro shot of a brass desk clock ticking softly against a blurred background with soft ambient shadows.

beats.say: Most people assume every dollar you send covers your interest first and chips away at your original debt.
beats.visual: A person's hands sorting through a stack of unopened envelopes on a dark kitchen counter with morning light.

beats.say: That is false. On income-driven plans, your monthly payment often only covers a fraction of the interest.
beats.visual: A close-up of a calculator on a wooden table with fingers resting quietly beside the plastic keypad.

beats.say: Where does all the leftover unpaid interest go every single month?
beats.visual: A stack of thick hardcover books resting on a dark shelf with dust motes drifting in a single beam of light.

beats.say: It doesn't vanish. It piles on top of your starting balance in a hidden loop called negative amortization.
beats.visual: An overhead shot of a person sketching lines on a grid notebook with a simple graphite pencil.

beats.say: Why does your total debt balloon even when you never miss a single due date?
beats.visual: A silhouette of a person standing by a large glass window looking out at a quiet city street at dusk.

beats.say: Because your interest compounds faster than your payment reduces it. The math works against your favor.
beats.visual: A slow pan across an empty leather chair in a quiet corner of a study lit by a floor lamp.

beats.say: Your student loan balance grows every month because your minimum payment is smaller than the monthly interest charge.
beats.visual: A close-up of a hand turning off a brass desk lamp, leaving the workspace in deep shadow.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A dark minimalist hallway with a single overhead light casting a clean line down the center floor.

caption: Why your student loan balance grows every month even when you make every payment on time. #studentloans #debtfree #moneyhacks #personalfinance #budgeting
description: Learn the math behind negative amortization in student loan income-driven repayment plans and why low minimum payments cause your total debt to balloon.
first_comment: Did your student loan balance surprise you this year? Drop your thoughts below.

facts.claim: Income-driven repayment plans can result in negative amortization where unpaid interest adds to the principal balance.
facts.basis: Standard federal student loan repayment rules for income-driven plans.
